e-3068.knowledge_point: Finding the Slope of the Tangent Line to a Curve at a Point
e-3068.problem: A surface $S$ is defined by $z=f(x,y).$ The curve $C$ is the intersection of $S$ with the plane $x=2.$ Given that the point $P(2,1,8)$ lies on $C,$ and that $f_y = \dfrac{4x}y - 4x^2y,$ find the slope of the tangent to $C$ at $P.$
e-3068.worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z=f(x,y)$ with the plane $x=2.$ So, the slope of the tangent to the curve $C$ at the point $P(2,1,8)$ will be given by the partial derivative $f_y(2,1).$

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative $f_y(x,y)$ at $(2,1)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(2,1) & =\frac{4(2)}{(1)}-4(2)^{2}(1) \\  & =8-16 \\  & =-8\end{aligned}
$$

e-3069.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of the Tangent Line to a Curve at a Point
e-3069.problem: The curve $C$ is the intersection of a surface $S,$ defined by $z=f(x,y),$ with the plane $y=\pi.$ Given that the point $P(1,\pi,-1)$ lies on $C,$ and that $f_x = y\cos(xy) + \cos y,$ find the equations of the tangent line to $C$ at $P.$
e-3069.worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z = f(x,y)$ with the plane $y=\pi.$ So, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $P(1,\pi,-1)$ will be given by the partial derivative $\dfrac {\partial z} {\partial x} \Bigg|_{(1,\pi)}.$ 

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative $\dfrac {\partial z} {\partial x}$ at $(1,\pi)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x}{|}_{(1,\pi )} & =\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(1\cdot \pi )+\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi  \\  & =\pi (-1)+(-1) \\  & =-\pi -1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-z{|}_{(1,\pi )} & =\frac{∂z}{∂x}{|}_{(1,\pi )}(x-1) \\ z-(-1) & =(-\pi -1)(x-1) \\ z+1 & =(-\pi -1)x+\pi +1 \\ z & =-(\pi +1)x+\pi \end{aligned}
$$

The equation above represents a line in the $xz$-plane. The $xz$-plane through the point $P(1,\pi,-1)$ has the equation $y=\pi.$

So, the tangent line to the curve $C$ at $P(1,\pi,-1)$ is given by the intersection of the following planes:

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=\pi  \\ z=-(\pi +1)x+\pi \end{aligned}
$$

a
{y=2z=−2x−π2

c
{y=2z=2x−2π
d
{y=2z=−2x+π
e
{y=2z=x+2π

decision.explanation: The slope is f_x(-π/2,2)=sin(-π/2)+(-π/2)(2)/π=-2. Point-slope form gives z-2π=-2(x+π/2), so z=-2x+π, with y=2.
